rainbow.name: Rainbow
rainbow.subtitle: A spectrum of small wins
rainbow.description: Give seven weeks of daily activity a little color. Every arc is a week; every segment is a day.
rainbow.encoding: 7 arcs × 7 days. Color intensity represents the value; pale gray means no data.

garden.name: Garden
garden.subtitle: Good habits take root
garden.description: Watch a month of effort grow into a garden. Three plants, thirty leaves, a story in every day.
garden.encoding: Each plant holds 10 consecutive dates. Leaf intensity represents value. A 31st day adds a sprout.

forest.name: Forest
forest.subtitle: See how your ideas grow
forest.description: Turn comparisons into a little woodland. A taller tree represents a larger value.
forest.encoding: Tree height represents value on a shared linear scale starting at zero.

river.name: River
river.subtitle: Find the flow in your data
river.description: Follow the gentle ebb and flow of your everyday rhythms, one observation at a time.
river.encoding: Vertical position represents value. Curves pass through observations without overshoot; gaps remain gaps.

bloom.name: Bloom
bloom.subtitle: A fuller picture, petal by petal
bloom.description: Give every dimension room to blossom. A simple flower reveals the shape of your strengths.
bloom.encoding: Petal length beyond the center represents value. Petal area is decorative, not a part-to-whole measure.

mountain.name: Mountain
mountain.subtitle: Make every milestone visible
mountain.description: Explore the peaks and quieter stretches of a journey, from daily activity to weekly demand.
mountain.encoding: Each vertex is an observation on a linear scale. Straight slopes connect adjacent values.

tide.name: Tide
tide.subtitle: Little by little, the tide rises
tide.description: A single goal, a rising tide. Make progress feel calm, tangible, and within reach.
tide.encoding: Water height represents the fraction of a target. Text preserves progress beyond 100%.

rings.name: Rings
rings.subtitle: Every season leaves a mark
rings.description: Layer your goals like the rings of a tree. Every circle has its own pace and possibility.
rings.encoding: Arc angle represents percent of each target. Compare angles or percentages, not raw arc lengths.

seed-ledger.name: Seed Ledger
seed-ledger.subtitle: Small things, counted carefully
seed-ledger.description: Count everyday wins as seeds, with an explicit unit and room for fractions.
seed-ledger.encoding: One seed represents a labeled denomination. Filled seed area represents a fractional unit; rows preserve exact totals.

waterline.name: Waterline
waterline.subtitle: Know when you reach the mark
waterline.description: Read capacity and meaningful thresholds on a calibrated water column.
waterline.encoding: Water height represents value on a linear zero-to-capacity scale. Dashed lines mark supplied thresholds. Fill caps at capacity; exact values remain.

sundial.name: Sundial
sundial.subtitle: Give your day a little sunlight
sundial.description: Arrange daily activities on a clock-time dial, with separate tracks for overlapping plans.
sundial.encoding: Angle represents 24-hour clock time. Arc extent represents duration. This is a schedule dial, not a physical sundial or solar calculation.

season-wheel.name: Season Wheel
season-wheel.subtitle: A whole year, in one glance
season-wheel.description: See real date intervals unfold around a Gregorian year, one season of work at a time.
season-wheel.encoding: Angle represents date within the selected year; arc extent represents duration. Month lengths and leap days are respected. No astronomical solar terms are calculated.

phenology.name: Phenology
phenology.subtitle: Readiness has its own rhythm
phenology.description: Follow observed milestones alongside expected windows, leaving unknown dates open.
phenology.encoding: Horizontal position represents date. Sprouts mark observed dates; shaded spans show expected windows; empty circles mean not observed.

lunar-cycle.name: Lunar Cycle
lunar-cycle.subtitle: Make room for a recurring rhythm
lunar-cycle.description: Arrange your own recurring routine around an abstract cycle with illustrative moons.
lunar-cycle.encoding: Angle represents cycle position; outer stem length represents value. Moon symbols are illustrative and do not encode completion or calculate lunar phase.

water-clock.name: Water Clock
water-clock.subtitle: Let time take a gentler shape
water-clock.description: Read elapsed or remaining duration through a calibrated vessel of water.
water-clock.encoding: Water height represents remaining duration in a constant-area vessel. Input convention is explicitly elapsed or remaining. This chart is a snapshot, not a timer.

balance.name: Balance
balance.subtitle: See both sides of the story
balance.description: Compare two quantities with common-scale bars and a softly tilting balance.
balance.encoding: Bar lengths use one linear scale. Beam tilt indicates the direction of the difference only; stones are decorative. Difference is right minus left.

cord-ledger.name: Cord Ledger
cord-ledger.subtitle: Every contribution has a place
cord-ledger.description: Count contributions on grouped cords, with a clear denomination for each knot.
cord-ledger.encoding: One knot represents a labeled denomination. Partial knot area represents a fraction. Parent tracks group contiguous cords. This is not a historical khipu decoder.

growth-history.name: Growth History
growth-history.subtitle: Let every chapter leave a trace
growth-history.description: Build a record of contributions as successive growth layers with a linked comparison view.
growth-history.encoding: Layer order follows input chronology. Ring thickness or area, as configured, represents period contribution; linked bars use a shared linear scale. Unknown periods have no quantitative layer.

tidal-rhythm.name: Tidal Rhythm
tidal-rhythm.subtitle: Find what returns, and what changes
tidal-rhythm.description: Compare repeating patterns as aligned cycles with a shared scale and honest gaps.
tidal-rhythm.encoding: Horizontal position represents position within each supplied cycle. Vertical position uses a shared numeric scale across cycles. Lines connect observations; this does not predict tides.

star-cycle.name: Star Cycle
star-cycle.subtitle: A constellation of things to return to
star-cycle.description: Give recurring checkpoints a place in a clearly labeled cycle.
star-cycle.encoding: Angular position represents cycle position. Star intensity represents value; exact values and cycle positions remain available. The arrangement is an abstract checkpoint map.

honeycomb.name: Honeycomb
honeycomb.subtitle: A place for every reading
honeycomb.description: Compare team activity across categories in a modular hexagonal heatmap.
honeycomb.encoding: Equal cells; intensity represents value. Rows are tracks; columns are labels.
honeycomb.rule: Up to 6 tracks × 6 labels, one observation per pair. Nonnegative values or null; absent cells are unmeasured.
honeycomb.inspiration: The modular hexagonal cells of bee and wasp nests.

mycelium.name: Mycelium
mycelium.subtitle: Connections beneath the surface
mycelium.description: Inspect dependencies, messages, or exchanges in a directed weighted network.
mycelium.encoding: Curved links connect source to destination; line width encodes weight. Nodes are identifiers, not quantities; long dashes mean zero and short dashes mean unknown weight.
mycelium.rule: Up to 18 directed links and 10 nodes. source and destination are required, distinct, and unique as a pair. Nonnegative values or null.
mycelium.inspiration: Adaptive biological networks, including fungal and slime-mold networks; no optimization is computed.

root-tree.name: Root Tree
root-tree.subtitle: Trace it back to the root
root-tree.description: Explore ownership, taxonomies, and parent-child dependencies.
root-tree.encoding: Depth follows parent links; node area represents its own value, never an inferred subtree total.
root-tree.rule: Up to 16 uniquely identified nodes, 4 depth levels, and at most 5 nodes per level. id is required; parent must exist; cycles are rejected. Nonnegative values or null.
root-tree.inspiration: Branching root systems and plant transport networks.

canopy.name: Canopy
canopy.subtitle: See the whole forest
canopy.description: Understand how departments and their projects contribute to one total.
canopy.encoding: Nested rectangles allocate area first to tracks, then to observations within each track.
canopy.rule: Up to 12 observations in at most 4 tracks. All quantities must be known and nonnegative. Zero-area contributions remain in the inspector.
canopy.inspiration: A canopy partitioned into neighboring crowns; rectangular areas are a modern abstraction.

fern.name: Fern
fern.subtitle: Find the few that matter
fern.description: Prioritize issue categories or costs using a Pareto view.
fern.encoding: Descending frond lengths show values; spores on a second axis show cumulative share.
fern.rule: Up to 8 known nonnegative quantities, sorted descending for display. Input indexes remain stable for callbacks.
fern.inspiration: A fern frond arranges repeated leaflets along a central stem.

phyllotaxis.name: Phyllotaxis
phyllotaxis.subtitle: Many parts, one seed head
phyllotaxis.description: Explain a portfolio, time allocation, or resource mix as one whole.
phyllotaxis.encoding: 120 equal dots follow a golden-angle spiral. Largest-remainder allocation approximates each category share.
phyllotaxis.rule: Up to 8 known nonnegative parts. Dots are rounded shares, not literal counts; exact totals remain in the table. All-zero data draws no allocated dots.
phyllotaxis.inspiration: Repeated seed placement in plant heads; this is a mathematical packing metaphor, not a claim about every species.

leaf-veins.name: Leaf Veins
leaf-veins.subtitle: Follow the change
leaf-veins.description: Compare before and after for several teams or measures.
leaf-veins.encoding: Paired endpoints share one linear axis: baseline is the old reading and value is the new reading.
leaf-veins.rule: Up to 6 observations. Every baseline must be finite. Signed readings and null new values are supported.
leaf-veins.inspiration: Veins connect two sides of a leaf; here they connect paired observations.

lotus.name: Lotus
lotus.subtitle: A profile with room to bloom
lotus.description: Compare performance across metrics with different target scales.
lotus.encoding: Each axis is value / target, capped at 100%; a dashed ring is the goal. Polygon shape depends on axis order.
lotus.rule: 3–8 nonnegative readings. Each positive target falls back to chart target or 100. Null readings break the polygon. Over-goal values stay exact.
lotus.inspiration: Radial arrangement of lotus petals; unlike Bloom, each axis has its own target.

petal-box.name: Petal Box
petal-box.subtitle: Let the spread unfold
petal-box.description: Compare variability and medians across groups using supplied quartiles.
petal-box.encoding: Whiskers span low–high; the petal body spans q1–q3; its line is the median (value).
petal-box.rule: Up to 6 known summaries satisfying low ≤ q1 ≤ value ≤ q3 ≤ high. These are supplied extrema, not automatically computed outliers.
petal-box.inspiration: A seed pod opening around its center inspires the distribution silhouette.

raincloud.name: Raincloud
raincloud.subtitle: See where readings gather
raincloud.description: Show a histogram from supplied, possibly unequal-width bins.
raincloud.encoding: Horizontal width is the bin interval. Height is frequency / bin width, so area represents frequency.
raincloud.rule: Up to 12 ordered, non-overlapping bins with low < high and known nonnegative frequencies. Gaps between bins remain gaps.
raincloud.inspiration: Rainfall falling from a cloud; frequency bars form the visible cloud profile.

dew.name: Dew
dew.subtitle: A clearer view of relationships
dew.description: Compare two numeric measurements and an optional third size variable.
dew.encoding: x is horizontal; value is vertical; optional weight controls droplet area. Hollow markers mean zero weight; dashed markers mean missing values.
dew.rule: Up to 40 readings with finite x. Signed values and null are supported. weight defaults to 1 and must be nonnegative. Missing readings sit in a separate rail.
dew.inspiration: Dew droplets provide small, distinct lenses onto individual observations.

wind-rose.name: Wind Rose
wind-rose.subtitle: Know which way it leans
wind-rose.description: Compare directional observations such as wind or arrival frequencies.
wind-rose.encoding: Equally spaced compass sectors use area proportional to value, with north at the top and clockwise angles.
wind-rose.rule: 4, 8, or 16 observations. angle must equal index × 360 / count. Nonnegative values or null. Values need not sum to 100.
wind-rose.inspiration: Compass directions and observed winds; no weather predictions are generated.

dune.name: Dune
dune.subtitle: Distributions across the landscape
dune.description: Compare supplied frequency profiles across cohorts.
dune.encoding: Each track has a ridge; position determines horizontal distance and height uses a common value scale.
dune.rule: Up to 4 tracks with 2–16 strictly increasing positions each. Nonnegative values or null; null breaks a ridge. Heights are supplied frequencies, not fitted densities.
dune.inspiration: Wind-shaped ridges in dune fields inspire the aligned silhouettes.

glacier.name: Glacier
glacier.subtitle: Every change leaves a step
glacier.description: Explain how gains and losses build a final balance.
glacier.encoding: Floating ice steps show signed contributions; their endpoints track the running sum from zero.
glacier.rule: Up to 10 known signed changes. Unknown changes are rejected because later cumulative totals would be unknowable.
glacier.inspiration: A stepped glacier landscape becomes a signed waterfall; it is not a glacier mass model.

sediment.name: Sediment
sediment.subtitle: Read the layers over time
sediment.description: Explore how a changing total is composed of several contributions.
sediment.encoding: Layer thickness is value at each position; stacked boundaries show the total on one linear scale.
sediment.rule: Up to 4 tracks sharing 2–16 identical increasing positions. All values must be known and nonnegative. Linear interpolation is visual, not extra observations.
sediment.inspiration: Deposited layers preserve sequences; chart thickness represents supplied contributions.

delta.name: Delta
delta.subtitle: One source, many paths
delta.description: Show how one budget or supply is allocated to destinations.
delta.encoding: One incoming ribbon splits into outgoing ribbons. Each width is proportional to its quantity.
delta.rule: Up to 7 known nonnegative links sharing one source and distinct destinations. Zero links remain inspectable.
delta.inspiration: River deltas branch a main channel into distributaries.

estuary.name: Estuary
estuary.subtitle: Meet where the currents join
estuary.description: Track transfers between several origins and destinations.
estuary.encoding: Bipartite ribbons have conserved widths; nodes show sums of their incident links.
estuary.rule: Up to 16 known nonnegative links with at most 5 sources and 5 destinations. Directed pairs must be unique. Left and right node sets are separate.
estuary.inspiration: River and sea exchanges inspire a modern many-to-many flow diagram.

pitcher.name: Pitcher
pitcher.subtitle: Where does the journey narrow?
pitcher.description: Locate attrition through a signup, sales, or completion funnel.
pitcher.encoding: Successive widths show remaining count relative to the first stage; labels show retention from the preceding stage.
pitcher.rule: 2–7 known nonnegative counts in non-increasing order. All-zero data has no measurable conversion percentage.
pitcher.inspiration: A pitcher plant’s narrowing chamber inspires the funnel silhouette.

firefly.name: Firefly
firefly.subtitle: See the moments light up
firefly.description: Spot bursts, pauses, and coincidences in event logs.
firefly.encoding: Horizontal position is event time; tracks separate event streams; glow intensity is magnitude.
firefly.rule: Up to 60 events in at most 5 tracks. position is required and may be irregular. Nonnegative values or null. Coincident events remain separate in the inspector.
firefly.inspiration: Brief firefly signals inspire discrete events, not an interpolated trend.

migration.name: Migration
migration.subtitle: A journey, stop by stop
migration.description: Show an ordered route through supplied coordinates.
migration.encoding: x and y locate each stop; arrows preserve input order; stop area represents value.
migration.rule: 2–20 known nonnegative readings, each with finite x and y. Coordinates are planar in the same unit, with equal scale on both axes; not projected latitude/longitude.
migration.inspiration: Animal migration inspires an ordered path; the chart does not infer a real route.

murmuration.name: Murmuration
murmuration.subtitle: Keep every individual in view
murmuration.description: Compare raw distributions across cohorts without binning away observations.
murmuration.encoding: Horizontal position represents value; vertical offsets separate nearby birds within each track and have no numeric meaning.
murmuration.rule: Up to 60 signed readings in at most 4 tracks. Null values use a separate rail. Crowded points may overlap; use the inspector for every record.
murmuration.inspiration: A flock remains many individual birds; each mark preserves one observation.

coral-range.name: Coral Range
coral-range.subtitle: Make uncertainty visible
coral-range.description: Compare estimates with supplied lower and upper bounds.
coral-range.encoding: Branch endpoints mark low and high; the central polyp marks value on a common numeric scale.
coral-range.rule: Up to 6 observations with finite low ≤ value ≤ high. A null center is allowed within a known range. These bounds are not assumed to be confidence intervals.
coral-range.inspiration: Branching coral provides a range silhouette; bounds remain application-defined.

pebble.name: Pebble
pebble.subtitle: Find your place in the stream
pebble.description: Read percentiles from a sample without choosing histogram bins.
pebble.encoding: A right-continuous step shows the empirical cumulative distribution; ties share the fraction at or below that value.
pebble.rule: Up to 60 known signed samples. All observations are retained, including ties. This is an empirical sample, not a fitted probability model.
pebble.inspiration: Pebbles accumulate downstream; each reading contributes equally to cumulative probability.

nautilus.name: Nautilus
nautilus.subtitle: Remember more than one turn
nautilus.description: Compare recurring work across several consecutive cycles.
nautilus.encoding: Angle represents position modulo cycleLength; spiral turn retains cycle number; dot area shows value.
nautilus.rule: Up to 36 nonnegative readings, strictly increasing positions from 0 to less than 4 × cycleLength. cycleLength defaults to 12.
nautilus.inspiration: Successive shell chambers inspire a spiral timeline; no biological growth law is inferred.

frost.name: Frost
frost.subtitle: Patterns in a crystal lattice
frost.description: Inspect a supplied correlation matrix with a fixed signed scale.
frost.encoding: Cells show values from −1 to +1; color distinguishes sign and intensity magnitude. Diagonal cells are one.
frost.rule: A complete symmetric matrix of 2–6 variables using track for row and label for column. Mirrored values must agree; symmetric null pairs are allowed.
frost.inspiration: A repeating crystalline lattice suggests symmetry; correlation never implies causation.

echo.name: Echo
echo.subtitle: Hear the previous reading
echo.description: Inspect lag-one dependence in an ordered numeric series.
echo.encoding: Each point pairs the preceding value on x with the current value on y; a diagonal marks equality.
echo.rule: 2–40 signed observations. Nulls break pairs. The first record has no predecessor and is shown in the inspector rail. No significance or causality is inferred.
echo.inspiration: Returning sounds inspire comparison with what came before; this is not an echolocation model.

cairn.name: Cairn
cairn.subtitle: Build toward one shared goal
cairn.description: Track which contributions make up progress toward a common target.
cairn.encoding: Stacked stone heights show contributions on a shared goal scale; the dashed line is the chart-level target, shared by every contributor.
cairn.rule: Up to 8 known nonnegative contributions and a positive chart target (default 100). The scale expands for over-goal totals; exact excess is retained.
cairn.inspiration: A cairn is assembled stone by stone; the stones here record contributions, not dates.

daylight.name: Daylight
daylight.subtitle: Watch the days open and close
daylight.description: Compare supplied sunrise/sunset or opening/closing windows across dates.
daylight.encoding: Each row shares a 24-hour axis; warm bands run from start to exclusive end; labels state duration.
daylight.rule: Up to 7 unique ISO dates with increasing HH:mm start/end in one day. Only end may be 24:00. No location or astronomical calculation is performed.
daylight.inspiration: Historical shadow observations motivated careful attention to changing daylight.

isobar.name: Isobar
isobar.subtitle: Connect equal readings
isobar.description: Explore a measured scalar field such as temperature or pressure.
isobar.encoding: Nodes retain measured values; lines interpolate equal values at 25%, 50%, and 75% of the observed range.
isobar.rule: Complete 2–8 by 2–8 grid of unique finite x/y coordinates and known finite values. Contours use piecewise-linear triangles; they are estimates between nodes.
isobar.inspiration: Isobars connect equal pressure; the same encoding works for other scalar fields.

bamboo.name: Bamboo
bamboo.subtitle: The original numbers, intact
bamboo.description: Inspect a compact integer distribution without losing exact readings.
bamboo.encoding: The stem is tens; each leaf is units. A key explains how to reconstruct the number.
bamboo.rule: Up to 60 integer values from 0 to 99, with at most 18 leaves per stem. Values are sorted within stems; repeated digits are distinct observations.
bamboo.inspiration: Segmented bamboo stems inspire a modern statistical stem-and-leaf plot, not an ancient invention.
